item: launch_server.ps1 writes the stop-asked row when the server ends with the Windows Ctrl-C status; the reader names it Ctrl-C (R168 parity)
summary: On exit -1073741510 the Windows wrapper appends one launcher_stops.jsonl row (schema, at, pid, boot_id null, signal null, status) after the server ended and trims it as the exit record is trimmed; the reader accepts a null-signal row only with exactly that status and reads it as Ctrl-C, stop requested, teardown incomplete, not a crash. The block is 313 B against the 384 B exit block it replaces. TESTED ONLY ON POWERSHELL 7 ON LINUX WITH A FAKE SERVER (the test runs a copy of the script with exit 58 in place of the NTSTATUS, since a Linux process cannot exit with one); PowerShell 5.1, cmd.exe and a real Windows console never run (same open list as the launcher-parity entry in OPEN_QUEUE.md).
